## Qualify the relationship before assigning the inquiry


Commercial solar inquiry qualification should establish the business identity, existing account relationship, and whether the requester is an end customer or an installation partner. These determine who should respond and which questions will advance the conversation. A company name or industry label alone does not establish the requester’s role in a specific project.


Start from the inquiry in HubSpot and search existing accounts and contacts. An installation partner may already have an owner, while an existing end customer may be asking about another facility. Preserve those relationships instead of creating a new prospect and routing it as an unrelated inbound lead.


Match the business: Use the inquiry’s business domain and existing HubSpot records to identify the company and relationship.; Establish the role: Determine whether this inquiry concerns the business’s own project or an installation partner’s customer.; Prepare the brief: Summarize the stated project, sourced business facts, relationship, and useful unknowns.

## Research the business and separate facts from project unknowns


Use the configured enrichment provider and business website to add sourced company information. Record source links and observation dates, and preserve verified CRM values when enrichment conflicts. Public information can establish what the business does, but it may not establish site ownership, project authority, financing, or procurement timing.


Read the actual inquiry for the requester’s role. Language about installing for clients suggests a partner conversation, while a request about the company’s own facility suggests an end-customer conversation. Treat those as evidence to interpret, not hard-coded conclusions that override an ambiguous message. Ask whether they are buying for their own operation or working on behalf of a customer when unclear.


## Route with a brief that prepares the first response


Apply existing account ownership and the organization’s approved end-customer or partner routing rules. Prepare a brief covering the requester, sourced company context, stated project, known relationship, unresolved role questions, and suggested follow-up. Keep a request awaiting clarification visible to an owner rather than silently assigning it to the wrong queue.


Tailor the questions to the role once established. An end-customer brief might ask which facility is in scope and who coordinates the project. A partner brief might ask the service area and whether the inquiry concerns a specific customer installation. Do not invent project capacity, incentives, estimated savings, or technical suitability from general company enrichment.


## A five-step operating sequence


1. 01


Match the business


Use the inquiry’s business domain and existing HubSpot records to identify the company and relationship. Preserve customer or partner ownership. A new project question should not erase a long-standing commercial relationship.


2. 02


Research public context


Read the configured enrichment provider and business website, adding sources for allowed company fields. Preserve verified values and distinguish estimates. Public context should prepare discovery, not establish unverified budget, project capacity, or purchasing authority.


3. 03


Establish the role


Determine whether this inquiry concerns the business’s own project or an installation partner’s customer. Ask for clarification when the message is ambiguous. A company’s industry classification is a clue, not a substitute for the requester’s project role.


4. 04


Apply owner rules


Route the inquiry using established account ownership and the approved end-customer or partner path. Keep any unresolved routing decision visible to the responsible team. Do not invent a territory or assign an unrelated owner to force completion.


5. 05


Prepare the brief


Summarize the stated project, sourced business facts, relationship, and useful unknowns. Choose discovery questions appropriate to the confirmed role. Avoid unsupported savings estimates, incentive eligibility, or technical conclusions about the proposed installation.


Qualify and Route Commercial Solar Inquiries in HubSpot — match the business, then research public context, then establish the role, then apply owner rules, then prepare the brief.


## Illustrative workflow example


An inquiry says the business wants equipment for a client’s warehouse. Existing HubSpot records show an installation-partner relationship. The workflow routes it to the partner owner with the project statement and questions about the customer installation scope.


This example uses fictional records to show the decision logic. It is not a customer case study or a claim of measured results. In a live case, retain the actual record IDs and evidence behind each statement, and replace all illustrative quantities or timing assumptions with the approved operational inputs.


## What the handoff should contain


A sourced HubSpot project brief with the requester’s confirmed role, existing relationship, correct owner, and role-specific follow-up questions.


Keep the evidence reference, observation time, current owner, and outstanding decision with the case. A colleague taking over should be able to distinguish a proposal from a confirmed result without reading every previous message. If a source value changes while the case is waiting, recheck the affected decision before proceeding.


Required systems feed case verification; missing evidence or decisions return to clarification before the workflow proceeds.


## Approval and completion checklist


-


Check existing account relationships before enrichment or routing.


-


Add sourced business information without treating estimates as verified project facts.


-


Determine end customer versus installation partner from the inquiry and clarify ambiguity.


-


Route to the appropriate owner with a brief and relevant follow-up questions.


## Validate the job before enabling it


Start with a small reviewed set of cases from the systems above. Include a complete case, an ambiguous match, a missing source record, and an interrupted action where the result is uncertain. Use a draft or test environment for validation and compare the output with the source records before allowing the configured production actions.


For this job, the most important checks are check existing account relationships before enrichment or routing. Route to the appropriate owner with a brief and relevant follow-up questions. Record the expected result before the trial, then compare both the proposed action and the final evidence. A fluent message is not a passing result if it skips one of these conditions.


-


Inquiries routed with an established requester role


-


Ambiguous roles clarified before final routing


-


Company attributes with recorded sources


Use these as operating measures, not promised performance improvements. Establish the current baseline and review exceptions with the team that owns the process. Investigate an increase in incorrect matches, unauthorized actions, or premature closure before expanding the job’s scope.
